items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: I called him to play piano with him. And then jobs he would get, he'd play piano and I would play banjo.

ctx.x: Where was the guy from and what did he do?

He was a trumpet player. And he was from Norco or someplace out there. But he lived here too. How about Hood? Did you know him? Douglas Hood? Hood, he played banjo and he played piano. Yeah, I mean him. Did he work with animals? Yes, indeed. Because a lot of jobs I would get. And I called him to play piano with him. And then jobs he would get, he'd play piano and I would play banjo. I'd like to see Hood. I hadn't seen him in so long. I don't know whether he's still alive or what. And uh, Eddie Johnson, I played…

Yeah. Well, so many of these fellows you're mentioning are two instrument players. Is this usual that they would have two instruments that they played? Well, yeah. Sometimes they'd have two banjos. No, I'm talking about, like for instance yourself, your banjo and guitar, the solo was piano and trumpet. Was this common that most musicians had at least two instruments that they played? Yeah, it was common. You see, a piano and a banjo, a piano and a guitar.
